title: Create a reusable custom entity
summary: Compose built-in geometry into a named entity with options, child ownership and a small public API.
outcome: Two labeled markers whose children share their parent transforms and whose captions respond to clicks.

blocks.text: A LabeledMarker owns a dot and a caption. The amber marker rotates as one object; click the cyan dot to change its caption. Begin with composition: the Entity parent carries shared state while the children supply rendering.

The constructor can run before the entity belongs to a scene. It creates CPU objects and uses compatible built-in components; it does not request a GPU device. Keep child creation here and expose deliberate setters for later changes.
2. Add the parent and manipulate it

Add the parent as the scene root. Its children remain owned by that parent. Moving or rotating the parent transforms the dot and caption together. The rendered dot receives the click event because the grouping parent supplies no pickable geometry of its own.

The complete source includes explicit package imports, camera setup, interaction and awaited animation. Use it as the starting file in your npm project. A custom geometry entity is the next level: compatible GeometryComponent, FragmentComponent and RendererComponent must agree on attributes, resources and shader layout. See [rendering architecture](/rendering-architecture).

Detaching a child with parent.remove does not destroy it. Scene.remove destroys the selected entity and its descendants. Release resources allocated by your own components in onDestroy; use [resource ownership](/lifecycle-resources) before adding buffers, textures or listeners. Entity cloning copies component state through the current clone implementation; custom owned resources need an explicit review before promising independent clones.

items: Add a third marker with another caption.
Move the caption locally, then rotate the parent and compare the result.
Change the public setter to update the dot color too.

blocks.text: Check the result: Both marker children should move together, and clicking cyan should change only its caption. If only one child moves, check which transform you changed.
Continue with [Create a custom component](/tutorial-custom-component). Use the [tutorial index](/tutorials) to choose another project.
